newsitem.title: CHINA: China challenges "unreasonable" EU dumping charges.
newsitem.headline: China challenges "unreasonable" EU dumping charges.

text.p: Beijing on Thursday denounced anti-dumping charges by the European Union against Chinese ferro-silico-manganese exports as unreasonable, saying Europe should stop seeing China as state-controlled economy.
A group of 12 Chinese producers and traders would send representatives to Brussels to defend themselves at a hearing on the anti-dumping charges on June 9, the official China Daily newspaper said.

China had not sold below-cost ferro-silico-manganese to Europe, it quoted Zhou Shijian, vice president of the China Chamber of Commerce of Metals, Minerals and Chemcials Importers and Exporters, as saying.
China's exceptionally low labour and operation costs and the fact that its producers did not have to pay for the environmental damage they caused meant prices were naturally low, Zhou said.

"Therefore, although the prices of Chinese ferro-silico-manganese are 'unbelievably' low as described by EU producers, Chinese producers and exporters can still gain considerable profits," the China Daily quoted him as saying.

Western media have said the European Commission opened an investigation into Chinese exports of ferro-silico-manganese, an alloy used in steel production, after local producers complained last year they were being undercut by Chinese pricing.
Imports from China had risen significantly in both absolute terms and in terms of market share, the European producers said.

Zhou said Chinese exports of the alloy to the EU were worth $80 million in 1995 and 1996, but that many EU factories had abandoned production of ferro-silico-manganese before China entered the market.
"Chinese exports of ferro-silico-manganese have not hurt the interests of EU producers," China Daily quoted him as saying.

The EU should abandon the practice of treating China as a state-controlled economy, a practice that means third country prices are used to determine if Chinese exporters are selling below cost, Zhou said.

"EU countries should learn from Australia, which decided on March 12 to treat China as a country in transition to a market-oriented economy and deal with anti-dumping actions against China case by case," he said.
